result.target_summary: Qualcomm's growth depends on extending technologies into new areas like automotive and IoT, but investments may not generate expected income, succeed due to patent/standard uncertainty, or yield returns due to underestimating costs, overestimating revenue, or long design cycles in regulated industries.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure D033 aggregates the same specific risks related to new initiatives as the five 2023 disclosures (D003-D007). D003 (general investment risks/patents) maps to D033 sentences P025-S01, P025-S02, P027-S01, P027-S02, P027-S03, P028-S01. D004 (automotive/ESG barriers) maps to D033 sentences P029-S01, P029-S02, P029-S03. D005 (product failure/standards) maps to D033 sentence P030-S01. D006 (business model/organization) maps to D033 sentence P031-S01. D007 (consequences of failure) is conceptually covered by the general risk statements in P025-S02 and the specific failure consequences in P028-S01/P030-S01/P031-S01 within the comprehensive D033 text. The underlying topic is identical: risks associated with expanding into new product areas like automotive and IoT.

previous_disclosures.summary: Investments in new and expanded product areas beyond mobile handsets, such as automotive and IoT, as well as in 5G and next-generation wireless technologies, may not generate expected operating income or returns due to risks including patent issuance failures, lack of standard adoption, slower market growth than anticipated, talent shortages, strategic misalignments, competitive pressures, and inaccurate cost or revenue estimates.

Entering the automotive industry involves significant barriers such as long design-in time frames, long product life cycles, stringent regulatory and safety requirements, and low defect rate standards. Additionally, customers may require achievement of sustainability, climate, or other ESG-related targets, such as the 2040 net-zero global GHG emissions commitment, and failure to meet these requirements may result in loss of customer purchases.

If products fail to perform to specifications, meet competitor quality levels, or comply with industry-specific safety, security, or ESG standards (which are particularly stringent in automotive), the company may be unable to expand business in those areas, limiting growth.
Extending technologies into new product areas may require transitioning to new business models or transforming organizational aspects, which may not be successful.

Failure to successfully extend technologies into new areas, lack of success for new technologies, or failure to meet anticipated time frames may result in significant costs, asset impairments, negative impacts on revenue and margins, stock price declines, and reputational harm.

comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Investment Risks and AI Technology Development
comparisons.peer_summary: Significant investments in research and development carry the risk of slow or unsuccessful returns, particularly in developing advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators and XPUs; failure to timely develop these or focus on non-adopted technologies could impair competitive position and negatively impact financial results.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO explicitly link the risk of new product area investments to the possibility that these investments will not generate expected income or operating results. QCOM notes that R&D in new areas 'may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.' AVGO states that 'the slow or unsuccessful return of our investments could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations,' specifically citing the development of advanced technologies like custom AI accelerators.

sentences.text: Our research, development and other investments in these new and expanded product areas, industries and applications, and related technologies and products, as well as in our existing technologies and products, and new technologies, may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.
We make investments in research and development and the slow or unsuccessful return of our investments could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

comparisons.peer_topic: New Market Competition and Investment Returns
comparisons.peer_summary: New businesses in AI, cloud-to-edge, and other areas introduce new competition and require significant investment with no guarantee of adequate returns. Failures in AI products or the foundry business could lead to asset impairments, restructuring charges, and opportunity costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and INTC identify the risk that significant investments in new product areas and emerging technologies may fail to generate expected returns. QCOM warns that R&D investments in areas like automotive and IoT 'may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.' Similarly, INTC states that developing products and market segments in areas like AI require 'significant investment' but 'do not always grow as projected or at all, or sometimes adopt competing technologies, and we may not realize an adequate return on our investments.'

sentences.text: Our research, development and other investments in these new and expanded product areas, industries and applications, and related technologies and products, as well as in our existing technologies and products, and new technologies, may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.

These developing products and market segments require significant investment, do not always grow as projected or at all, or sometimes adopt competing technologies, and we may not realize an adequate return on our investments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Innovation efforts involve significant expense with no guarantee of expected benefits from next-generation process technologies. If returns are inadequate, Intel may be required to write down manufacturing assets and facilities, as occurred in the third quarter of 2024 for the Intel 7 process node.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the risk that innovation and new technology development involve substantial costs with no guarantee of success or adequate capital returns. QCOM states its 'research, development and other investments... may not generate operating income.' INTC elaborates on this by noting that efforts to innovate 'involve significant expense and carry inherent risks' and that they 'cannot guarantee that we will... achieve an adequate return on our capital and R&D investments,' potentially requiring write-downs of manufacturing assets.

sentences.text: Our research, development and other investments in these new and expanded product areas, industries and applications, and related technologies and products, as well as in our existing technologies and products, and new technologies, may not generate operating income or contribute to future results of operations that meet our expectations.

We cannot guarantee that we will realize the expected benefits of next-generation process technologies, including the expected cost, performance, power, and density advantages, or that we will achieve an adequate return on our capital and R&D investments, particularly as the development of new nodes has grown increasingly expensive.

peer_results.rationale: MU's candidates focus on capital expenditure return uncertainty and ESG goals. While capital expenditure risk is related, MU's disclosure centers on construction delays and judgment in selecting projects rather than the specific R&D/product development risks and technology adoption uncertainties inherent in QCOM's new product area investments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Requirements for success in adapting to industry changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Success depends on timely adaptation to industry changes, R&D investments, launching new business models like cloud solutions, expanding ecosystems, managing lifecycles, securing infrastructure, and making necessary investments.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and NVDA frame their future growth and success as dependent on the ability to develop and adapt to new technologies and industry changes through R&D. QCOM states, 'Our growth depends in part on our ability to extend our technologies and products into new and expanded product areas.' NVDA mirrors this dependency, stating, 'Our success depends on our ability to... timely identify industry changes... and develop new or enhance and maintain existing products and technologies,' including through 'investments in research and development.' Both highlight that failure in these new areas poses a risk to their core business trajectory.
